newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Skoda wins San Francisco trolley order.
newsitem.headline: Skoda wins San Francisco trolley order.

text.p: Czech heavy engineering group Skoda a.s. said on Tuesday that it had won an order from the U.S. city of San Francisco for trolley buses in a contract totalling over five billion Czech crowns ($170.1 million).
In a statement, Plzen-based Skoda said the projected total for the order had yet to be finalised, with details of the supply plus financial and technical conditions.
That is expected to be completed by mid-year, it said.

"We consider victory in this tender to be an extraordinary success not only in view of the expected volumes of supplies... but also because the U.S. market is among the most prestigious and demanding in the world," Skoda spokesman Jaroslav Hudec said in a statement.
He said this contract would open the way for Skoda to acquire more contracts in the United States and establish the company's brand name.
The statement said that the contract meant the largest supply of Czech goods to the United States in the entire trading history of the two countries.

Earlier this decade Skoda won a contract to supply 54 trolley buses to the city of Dayton, Ohio, and founded a U.S. joint venture with private partners in Baltimore, Electric Transit International (ETI), to assemble the buses.
Skoda a.s. is no longer affiliated with the Czech car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s., now a unit of Volkswagen AG.
